covers: Provider objection: every check passes, but the provider objected, so the request must still be flagged
title: Employee wage records for contribution audits
objection: We object because the request covers every establishment rather than only those selected for audit.

F-R1.quote: To check that the contributions employers pay are calculated on the wages they actually paid their employees.

F-R2.quote: PDPL Article 15(3): disclosure requested by a public entity to implement another law, namely the Social Insurance Law.

F-R3.quote: Collecting social insurance contributions on the correct wage base, a function given to the Organization by the Social Insurance Law.

F-R4.quote: Employee name, national ID number, employer establishment number, monthly wage paid.

F-R5.quote: Kept for five years after the related contribution audit is closed, then destroyed.

F-R6.quote: Requested by the General Organization for Social Insurance from the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development.

F-P1.quote: Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development, Data Management Office, privacy@hrsd.example

F-P2.quote: Monitoring private-sector wage payments under the wage protection programme to enforce timely and correct payment of wages, and confirming wages paid to the General Organization for Social Insurance for contribution audits.

F-P3.quote: Processing required to implement the Labour Law.

F-P4.quote: Employee name, national ID number, employer establishment number, monthly wage paid, bank account number the wage was paid into, payment date.
items: bank account number the wage was paid into

F-P5.quote: Private-sector employees whose wages are paid through the wage protection programme.

F-P6.quote: The General Organization for Social Insurance, for contribution audits; other government entities where a law requires disclosure.

F-P7.quote: No transfer or disclosure outside the Kingdom.

F-P8.quote: Wage payment records are kept for ten years after the payment date.
